texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are that on 07.11.2021, upon receipt of information through DD no. 41A regarding flipping of a vehicle near Khanna Market, Lodhi Road, investigating officer reached the spot where one vehicle Eicher Tempo bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was found flipped on the middle of the road. The person injured had been taken to the hospital by then. On reaching the hospital, one of the injured Ganesh Das stated that on 07.11.2021 at 03:00 p.m., he was travelling along with 12 other people in the offending vehicle. After performing religious ritual (idol immersion) near Yamuna River, at Sarai Kale Khan, all the 13 passengers boarded the offending vehicle for returning to Bengali Camp. When the offending tempo reached near Najaf Khan Tomb, Najaf Khan Road, Lodhi Road, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 started driving the vehicle at very high speed recklessly. Despite being cautioned he kept driving the vehicle negligently at high speed, due to which the offending Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date: 04:29:32 +0530 MACT No. 323/22 Yash Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 2 of 24(ss) vehicle flipped off, causing injury to its passengers and death of the son of the petitioner. 3. An FIR No. 206/2021 dated 07.11.2021 u/s 188/279/269/337/338/304A of IPC & Section 3 Epidemic Disease Act was registered at PS Lodhi Colony. Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, is owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. In response to the DAR, insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle. It is further pleaded that even the injured Yash Das was found to be under influence of alcohol. It is pleaded that since the offending vehicle could be used only as a light goods carriage vehicle, petitioner was an unauthorized /gratuitous passenger along with 12 other persons, all of whom were in violation of the Covid-19 pandemic (DDMA guidelines) guidelines and thus not entitled to compensation. It is further pleaded that there is a possibility that the offending vehicle may have been planted to raise a false claim. Despite opportunity, no reply was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 or respondent no.2. 5. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.01.2023. 1) Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA OPP. 3) Relief. 6. In the present case no separate evidence has been led by injured Yash Das , however, it is observed that as per the report filed by Ld.LC, a common evidence has been recorded in all the 13 connected cases of victims as witnesses therein. 7. In respondent evidence, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 as RW1 Akendra Kumar led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R1W1/A. In his examination in chief, he stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident. He denied any rash or negligent act on his part in driving of the offending vehicle. He stated that the petitioner/victims have falsely implicated him and that FIR no. 206/21 has been lodged with a motive to extort money from the respondents. He stated that none of the alleged victims were travelling in the offending vehicle. He relied upon his identity card as Ex.R1W1/1. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. Such cross examination was adopted by ld. Counsel for petitioners. Respondent no.2/owner also examined himself as RW2/Sh. Bhanu Prakash Sharma. He led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R2WA and his identity card as Ex.R2W2/1. RW2 also denied involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and pleaded the FIR to be false and concocted. He asserted that the liability to pay compensation, if any, lies upon the insurance CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 04:29:42 +0530 MACT No. 323/22 Yash Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 4 of 24(ss) company with which his vehicle was insured. 8. Insurance company /respondent no.3 also examined its witness Sh. Parth Arya as R3W1. R3W1 led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/1 wherein he testified that as per the Registration Certificate, the offending vehicle was a light goods vehicle with a seating capacity of 3 persons. He stated that the said vehicle was being used for transportation of passengers, beyond its permitted capacity, in violation of the permit. He testified that since the respondent no.1 and 2 committed breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by violating the RC and permit, the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. He relied upon his authority letter as Ex.R3W1/1, attested copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/3 and DAR /FIR /chargesheet/RC/Route Permit as already Ex.PW1/6 (colly). Total compensation after deduction Rs.12,000/- Interest: Simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till actual realization of Award amount/ compensation. 22. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.12,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization.
